clue.text: View recording result of The Birds' rear attack?

indicators.note: a recording captures what is heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.words: result of The Birds' rear attack
parts.note: birds attacking from behind leave droppings, so a car would end up a specked one

explanation.surface: A viewer recalls the damage done in Hitchcock's film when the birds strike from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recording' signals a homophone: 'a specked' (spattered with spots by bird droppings) is said like the answer. The Birds is Hitchcock's film.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook or prospect from a building is a synonym of a view.

clue.text: Irish statesman raved drunkenly about beer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters enclose the drink
something done drunkenly is done in a muddle, so the letters of raved are jumbled

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A politician from Ireland rants after too many pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' turns RAVED into DEVRA; 'about' puts that round ALE, splitting it as DEV...RA. Eamon de Valera led Ireland for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamon de Valera was Taoiseach and later President of Ireland, a leading political figure.

clue.text: Prepare to broadcast upcoming festival of poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tide is an old poetic word for a feast or festival, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Someone gets a poetry festival ready to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reverses TIDE in this down clue. 'Festival of poetry' looks like an eisteddfod, but it means 'festival' in poetic language.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing material is getting it ready for publication or transmission.

clue.text: Critical time for action almost over, matter arising is consistent

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the shortened word is read backwards
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: D-Day is the day set for a major operation to begin

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound

explanation.surface: A deadline nearly past, with an issue coming up, still holds together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DDAY to DDA, which 'over' turns to ADD; 'arising' turns PUS to SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that adds up makes sense, the idiom for being coherent.

clue.text: What's rising notoriety on island in curtailment of friendlier relations

indicators.note: in means placed inside the shortened word
curtailment means docking a tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a thaw is an easing of hostility between parties

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: fame here means being widely known, notoriety

explanation.surface: A clue asks what is gaining infamy on an island where warmer relations are being cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FAME to EMAF; 'curtailment of' cuts THAW to THA; 'in' puts EMAF + I inside it as TH...A. The definition rests on Cosa Nostra, literally 'our thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian crime syndicate calls itself Cosa Nostra, literally 'our thing', so the organisation is a 'what'.

clue.text: Puff of vapour emanating from women behind

parts.note: aft means towards the rear, nautically

explanation.surface: A whiff of steam drifts from a group of women at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A light current of scent or air drifting along is a waft.

clue.text: What viewers see when "Thunderbirds are Go"?

definitions.text: What viewers see when "Thunderbirds are Go"?

parts.words: What viewers see when "Thunderbirds are Go"?
parts.note: the TV series was filmed with marionettes hung on strings, so viewers watched moving figures dangling in the air

explanation.surface: A fan describes the screen when the famous puppet show's catchphrase rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: Thunderbirds was a 1960s British puppet adventure series filmed in 'Supermarionation'. The phrase usually means a state of halted life, but here it is read literally: hanging puppets brought to life.
explanation.definitionFit: The puppets hang on wires and are made to move, a literal reading of the phrase for a body's halted vital functions.

clue.text: It's imparted in pre-16 time, so country dance idea may work

indicators.note: the letters may be worked into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher proposes a country dance as a school lesson plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may work' signals an anagram of all eighteen letters of SO COUNTRY DANCE IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: British schooling from about eleven to sixteen is the stage after primary, taught in high schools.

clue.text: Giggle about a backsliding scoundrel's problem

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the giggle goes round the rest

parts.note: hee-hee is the sound of a giggle
taken as written

indicators.note: sliding back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a relapsing rogue's trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' turns CAD into DAC; 'about' puts HE...HE round A + DAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of trouble or worry is called a pain or nuisance.

clue.text: See 8
In advance is Issue One intolerant of things Jewish?

indicators.note: In placed first means the following pieces go inside

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance
taken as written
to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: A question about whether the first edition published is prejudiced against Jewish matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts IS + EMIT inside ANTE, splitting it as ANT...E. 'One' belongs to the definition, not to the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hostile to Jewish people and their culture is a bigot of this kind.

clue.text: More of the same, vicar, or something completely different?

definitions.meaning: a vicar's hospitality: a refill of the tea already served
a different kettle of fish, an idiom for a quite separate matter

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a refill of the brew; figuratively the idiom 'a different cup of tea' means a separate matter entirely.

clue.text: Cloth patch in old dress

indicators.note: the letters are dressed in the surrounding words, which clothe the answer

explanation.surface: A patch of fabric is sewn into an old frock.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through patCH IN Old.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a sturdy twilled cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: See 7
"New Age", as in the clue "A medieval group"

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter explains that a New Age movement appears in a clue about a medieval body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' signals an anagram of AGE AS IN THE CLUE A, fifteen letters, which reads like a playful self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanseatic League was a trading alliance of north German towns in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Top facility promoted US No 2, getting Queen quids in

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved upwards, so US reads bottom to top
in means set inside the euphemism

parts.note: number two is a childish euphemism for poo
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen
L stands for pounds, the British quid

explanation.surface: A top lavatory rises to second place in America, with royal money pouring in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns US into SU; 'in' puts ER + L inside POO as P...OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A superloo is a high-tech automated public toilet, so a facility of the best kind.

clue.text: Spartan and blue one Christmas, looking to the skies?

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking skywards means the run is read upwards

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits
I is the Roman numeral one
Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A gloomy Christmas leaves someone gazing up at a meteor shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking to the skies' reverses the whole run SADINOEL; the Leonids meteor shower adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonidas was the king of Sparta who fell at Thermopylae.

clue.text: Olympic goals? Divers including Daley exploring reasons for flaws?

indicators.note: including means the extra name joins the letters
divers is an old word for various, so the letters go every which way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Tom Daley is a British Olympic diver

explanation.surface: Olympic aims of divers, Tom Daley among them, being studied for weaknesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the athletes but means 'various', the anagram signal; 'including' adds TOM, for Tom Daley, the British diving champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Symptomology is the study of the signs that point to a disorder.

clue.text: Annoyed about forgetting name eventually

indicators.note: about signals rearranging and forgetting says a letter goes missing from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone is cross at forgetting a name in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one N from ANNOYED and rearrange OAYEDN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at some future time, sooner or later.

clue.text: Gradually establish permanency, carrying bat not quite to the end

parts.note: in cricket an opener carrying the bat is not out, so still in

indicators.note: the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: still describes something lasting or continuing, permanency

explanation.surface: A batsman builds a lasting innings without quite reaching the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite to the end' cuts STILL to STIL. In cricket, an opener who 'carries the bat' is still not out, i.e. IN, at the end of the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to implant an idea or habit slowly over time.

clue.text: One in/excluded from residence, order required?

definitions.text: One in/excluded from residence, order required?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word residence
the letters need to be put in order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A divorcing partner is asked to leave the marital home by court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' adds I to RESIDENCE and 'order required' rearranges the ten letters. The whole clue is the definition: the court order that leads to a divorce, after which one partner moves out.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is the provisional court order in a divorce, before the final decree absolute.

clue.text: Twin negotiator of relative order for soup and dash of Worcestershire sauce

definitions.text: Twin negotiator of relative order for soup

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, so only a few letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A biblical brother trades for broth, with a splash of Worcestershire sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through worcestershirE SAUce. In Genesis, Esau sells his birthright (rights as elder twin, 'relative order') to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau, Jacob's twin, sold his birthright for a serving of pottage.

clue.text: I want a lot in the same place

parts.note: at auction you bid for a lot you want

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a great deal in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want a lot' looks like 'desire much', but a lot is an auction item.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin footnote word meaning the source just cited.
